first_impression: This is a lot more game than a one-line itch page made me expect: a nine-evening season map, charms, a second dog, a ram, a trial, mist, a storm, snow and a night watch. The golden title shot and the low view by the bridge are genuinely lovely, but most of the time I am looking down from very high at tiny cotton balls on a field, and once the sun goes down the ground turns into a muddy purple-orange smear.
best_things: The low tilted view at 00:50-01:02 (Pip in the foreground, the stream and wooden bridge behind, sheep crossing the stepping stones) is the screenshot that sells the game, and the sunset cutaways at 00:27 and 11:55 have real atmosphere.

Every evening adds a real twist I can see on screen: Fly the older dog at 03:00-04:20, Old Angus the horned ram leading the ewes at 05:40, mist with bleat icons at 07:35, the flooded ford in the storm at 10:42, the black sheep in the snow at 11:30, and a night watch that ends at dawn at 16:00.

The wolf threat is easy to read when it matters: the red toothed ring round the wolf, the red banner with distance and seconds to save the sheep, the little inset camera of the snatch (07:10, 10:30, 14:00) and the 'Sheep rescued!' payoff (07:22, 14:15) make a clear little drama.

worst_problems.problem: After sunset the ground stops looking like a place and becomes a smeared purple and orange gradient with big dark blotches over it; at Crannach Corrie the lake edge sits under a black smudge and the heather turns neon violet, so the evening I most want to admire looks like a bruise.
worst_problems.where: 06:27-07:30 (corrie), 04:40-05:27 (Loch Ailsa dusk), 07:15 (dark blotch over the lake during the snatch)
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the ground's own colours and let the sunset be in the light and the sky; lose the dark patches that look like dirt on the lens.

worst_problems.problem: The Glenbrae Trial is about 90 seconds of one flat mustard-green field with a few red hurdles, the camera straight down, five sheep shuffling slowly; nothing else moves or changes, and it is the second evening I would play.
worst_problems.suggestion: Give the show field life in the play camera (crowd, bunting, a judge, a sheepdog commentator line, the next gate called out) and a faster, tighter course so it feels like a competition, not a lawn.

worst_problems.problem: Mist on the Moor is a washed-out beige screen with a slightly less washed-out circle round Pip; sheep, bridge and wolves are all ghosts and for over a minute nothing much happens but Pip walking along a ditch.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the mist darker and moodier with more contrast inside the clear area, and put something to find in it more often (a lost sheep, a wolf shape, a landmark) so the blindness creates tension instead of boredom.

worst_problems.problem: The herding camera is so high and far out that Pip and the sheep are tiny and the movement has no weight; the running, the flock bunching and the bark all read as small icons sliding on a big field, and the beautiful close view is used only for a few seconds.
worst_problems.suggestion: Sit the default camera lower and closer, or let me play from the tilted view more of the time, and add a bit more squash, dust and reaction when the flock breaks and turns.

worst_problems.problem: The storm, and then the Wolf Moon replay of the same storm, are a long grey-violet blur under rain with near-identical far-bank snatches one after another, the same red banner each time, and a full white flash frame; the HUD (tiny counter text, chips, minimap, banners) piles up on top.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the Wolf Moon replay look and play differently (a red moon, new routes), vary the wolf events, soften the lightning flash, and make the HUD text bigger and quieter.

boredom_points: The Glenbrae Trial at 01:27-02:55: same yellow field, same slow push, minute after minute.
The mist at 08:30-09:12, walking along a ditch in a beige fog with nothing happening.
The Wolf Moon storm at 13:15-15:17 feels like replaying the storm I just saw, with the same far-bank snatch banners on a loop.
confusions: The night watch jumps from a blue moonlit night (15:42, 'Dawn in 3:36') to a warm golden dusk (15:45, 'Dawn in 0:38'); I could not tell if time skipped or if dawn really looks like sunset.
The top-left counter is a row of tiny dots and stars that I could not read at a glance; I had to rely on the banners to know whether I was winning.
The second dog Fly is red-brown and from above looks a lot like a wolf or a fox at 03:15 and 04:50, especially next to a real wolf ring.
Small round icons at the screen edges (bleat speech bubbles, house markers, red wolf badges) all look alike at this size.
wish_list: A camera option to play from the low tilted view, or a closer default.
More life in the world while herding: other farm animals, birds, the farmer at the gate, weather that changes mid-evening.
Commands to give Fly beyond 'lie down', so the two-dog evenings feel like real teamwork.
A proper trial scoreboard and replays, maybe a daily trial leaderboard.
A photo mode for the sunset and snow scenes.
one_line_review: A cosy, surprisingly deep sheepdog season with real variety and a lovely golden hour, held back by a too-distant camera, a muddy purple dusk and a couple of dull evenings.
